issues.status: overbroad claim contradicted by inspected code
issues.before: iCloud, Google Calendar and Microsoft Outlook, synced two ways and colour-coded in a single view. Toggle any calendar off when you don’t want to see it — the rest keeps working.
issues.proposed: View selected iCloud and Google calendars together; Premium adds Microsoft calendars. Edit where your account permissions allow, and check the source calendar after changes.
issues.reason: Direct outbound/inbound paths exist, but read-only calendars, selected-calendar filtering and provider errors defeat blanket two-way/rest-working wording. Hiding a calendar affects more than rendering, including Google uploads and notification input.

issues.status: overbroad claim contradicted by inspected code
issues.before: Grab an event and slide it to a new time or a different day. Pull its top or bottom edge to change how long it runs. No modal, no save button.
issues.proposed: Move editable events to another time or day, or resize them in the timeline. For a repeating event, choose which occurrences to change and review the saved result.
issues.reason: Recurring EventKit edits explicitly show an action sheet; read-only events rejected. Do not replace with claim all gestures need manual save.

issues.status: overbroad claim contradicted by inspected code
issues.before: That is the main way to edit. Drag an event to another time or another day, or pull its top or bottom edge to change the duration. Changes sync straight back to the source calendar.
issues.proposed: You can move editable events and resize them in the timeline. Check the recurrence choice and saved time; connected-calendar updates depend on permissions and successful synchronization.
issues.reason: Straight back implies reliable immediate provider success. Gesture/UI save and provider acceptance are separate. No evidence supports main way as user behavior.

issues.status: overbroad claim contradicted by inspected code
issues.before: The same events, arranged for the question you are actually asking — and every one of them carrying the forecast.
issues.proposed: Choose an overview or a detailed timeline, with available weather alongside supported views.
issues.reason: Forecast data finite; year mini-view has no weather data input. Every event/view carrying forecast is unsupported.

issues.status: overbroad claim contradicted by inspected code
issues.before: An hourly grid where every row carries its own forecast. You see the 3pm meeting and the 3pm rain in the same glance — no second app, no guessing.
issues.proposed: Compare appointments with available hourly weather in the same grid. Check the selected place and forecast date when planning outdoors.
issues.reason: Every row/no guessing overstates finite returned weather and forecast uncertainty.

issues.status: overbroad claim contradicted by inspected code
issues.before: Month view marks every day that has something on it. Year view puts twelve months on one screen — the fastest way to find a free week.
issues.proposed: Compare selected-calendar events across the month or year. Open a day to inspect all its appointments before deciding that it is free.
issues.reason: Selection and underlying available data limit overview; visible free week not proven availability. Month chips truncate. Fastest has no comparison evidence.

issues.status: overbroad claim contradicted by inspected code
issues.before: Tap any hour in the weather hub and a new event opens, already set to that time. Find the dry window, then book it.
issues.proposed: Choose an available forecast hour to start an event draft, then review its date, time and calendar before saving.
issues.reason: Calendar permission required; draft not saved booking. Main hourly callback supplies today; avoid universal any-hour/date claim. This aligns existing weather.tapAnHour copy.

issues.reason: Source supports tracked invite refresh, not universal automatic updates for any shared copy; released behavior of current tree not established. Version-specific feature claim needs release-note evidence.

issues.proposed: On iPhone or iPad, open Settings, tap your name, then Subscriptions. Choose Cloud Calendars and cancel there; check the cancellation or expiry status shown by Apple.
issues.reason: Official current Apple instructions are Settings > name > Subscriptions. No blanket future charge guarantee needed; confirm resulting status.
